Episode 124: Elders in Crisis (6)
Swoosh!
Sigmund's blade sliced through Rok's bones and flesh, making a sharp sound.
Rok was not originally the type to be dealt with so easily, but the result of focusing only on Lata was disastrous.
He tried to react and dodge late, but blood was already gushing from the severed leg.
"Argh...!"
Losing a leg meant the fight was as good as over.
Jin leisurely cut off Rok's other leg, then turned his gaze to Laks, who was barely holding onto his soul.
"Please treat him so he doesn't die, Sir Lata."
"How dare you, Rok!"
"How dare I? Do you know who I am, and yet you carelessly blabber such nonsense, Laks Seigal?"
Vroom-!
Jin's charging blade fell to Laks' forehead. Laks reacted easily to the strike, but was shocked by the force pressing down on his blade.
'What power!'
After exchanging just one blow, his wrist trembled, and the muscles holding his stance felt like they were about to tear.
Just who was this person? That question crossed Laks' mind for a moment.
Fzzzt-!
Lightning sparked from the blue, hazy Sigmund's blade.
Until a few years ago, lightning had symbolized the contractors of Phaytel, but not anymore.
Jin Runcandel, the lightning bursting from his sword, was now his symbolic power.
"Jin Runcandel...!"
"If you recognize me, then quietly accept my blade."
The Sword of the King's lightning fell above Laks' head. As a warrior who had reached a certain level, Laks showed a flexible response to the unfamiliar attack.
But that was all.
From the beginning, Jin's swordsmanship was far superior to Laks'. As soon as the offense and defense began, Laks was only being pushed back.
"So you really became Runcandel's dog, Lata Proch!"
Lata roughly stopped the bleeding from Rok's leg and shrugged his shoulders.
"It seems the traitors have passed on the wrong message, Laks. It's similar but a bit different. I decided to become not Runcandel's dog, but Jin Runcandel's dog."
"You shameless bastard."
"Shame? In the mercenary world, losing is the greatest shame. You and the elders made the wrong choice, and you're just paying the price."
Laks glared and lunged at Lata, but Jin easily blocked his way.
Kagagang!
Sigmund and his sword clashed, creating sparks.
It was not only impossible to win but also impossible to escape. Laks Seigal had no choice but to quickly come to that conclusion.
"Laks Seigal. We just met as enemies, and so far, there's no other emotion involved. So if you just answer a few of my questions, I'll let you go without pain."
"It's bad enough that the throne was taken by a monster named Smarion that appeared out of nowhere. I never thought I'd hear such words from the likes of a 12th-generation Runcandel."
"Should I take it as a refusal to accept my proposal?"
As Jin asked, some of the captains who had been heading in the other direction entered the Seigal brothers' room.
"Lord! We've caught them."
The captains had captured the traitorous elders from another room. They had been treated with poison, so they could barely speak.
Lata's eyes shone with murderous intent as he looked down at the elders.
"You old rats... Did you think you could defy me and live? Moreover, you were colluding with Seigal and looking for other forces to join."
Naturally, the betrayal of the ghostly elders did not affect Jin emotionally.
However, for Lata, their betrayal could only have been a significant shock. The elders were not only members of the Seigal family, but they had also shared hardships with Lata for a long time.
"Thanks to you, my lord had to deal with the risk factors of the Ghost Legion as soon as the alliance was formed. So from now on, answer my questions sincerely."
Lata continued speaking as he sat Roks next to the elders.

"First, which force did you choose? Second, did you inform them of the alliance between me and my lord and the secrets of Gyegok Bird Fortress? If your answers are insincere, not only you but also your innocent relatives, family members, and even the dogs you raise will be skinned and killed one by one."
It was not an empty threat. Lata was a man who could do more than that.
"Puhahaha..."
Silence lingered for a moment, and then one of the captured elders suddenly burst into laughter.
"Lata Proch! Do you think killing our family and relatives would cause us great pain?"
"What?"
"What do you think, Jin Runcandel? If we were afraid of that, would we have left Gyegok Bird Fortress?"
Not only the elders, but also Laks Seigal had a smirk on his face.

"Lata, you just said it to me. Roks, the elders, and I made the wrong choice and are paying the price. Losing is the most shameful thing in the mercenary world. That's right... Your words are not wrong."
Laks spoke with a more composed voice as he caught his breath.
The face filled with strange confidence, Jin felt like he had seen that kind of expression somewhere before.
"However, are we really the ones who made the wrong choice?"
"Laks Seigal, what nonsense are you babbling?"
"What I mean is, in the end, the one who will pay the price is not us, but you. Runcandel? You're wrong, Lata."
Despite being in a desperate situation, the Seigal brothers and the elders showed a defiant attitude. There was no sign of humiliation or meanness.
What lay behind them was not courage or pride.
Jin made such a judgment intuitively. And suddenly, one person came to mind.
'Barton Vichena.'
The only black knight who betrayed Runcandel and sided with Zipfel.
His last appearance was like this.
-Even if you kill me today, there's an unchanging truth. First, if the Chiron disappears, Runcandel will surely perish. Second, even if my body is destroyed, I can exist longer than you.
-By that time, you will have no choice but to admit that Barton Vichena's choice was not wrong.

Seigal and the traitorous elders had the same look in their eyes as Barton did that day. A look that could only be held by those who believed they had entered a world where death had lost its meaning.
"Zipfel, huh?"
When Jin opened his mouth, everyone's gaze gathered.
"You joined Zipfel and leaked information. And you must have been promised eternal life or transcendent power from them. So you're not afraid of death now."
Jin, holding his sword, stared at Laks.
"But do you know? There was someone who told me the same thing before. To him, I told the story of how my sister and I shattered the Devil's Stone."
As the word 'Devil's Stone' was mentioned, the Seigal brothers and the elders flinched.
"So... it's better not to trust the Devil's Stone too much. If that stone had such omnipotent power in the first place, it wouldn't make sense for you to die here. Lord Lata."
"Yes, my lord."
"There is no more information to find out. Kill them all."
As Lata nodded, Laks glared at Jin.
"Give me a gift, Jin Runcandel."
"No need..."
Ziiiing!
Suddenly, red glowing runes appeared all over Laks' body. The same happened to the captured Roks and the elders.
And Jin and Lata had seen something very similar to those red runes not long ago.
'The seal that's trapping Smarion... It's the same...!'
Passed down only to the elders of the Ghost Legion for generations, a seal that uses the life of the drinker as a material.
The remnants of the Seigal were trying to unleash that seal for the last time. Roks and Laks had already learned this seal from the elders who betrayed Lata long ago.
"You'll end up like your father, Lata!"
"Are these madmen... going to kill even their own servants?"
At Lata's question, Laks let out a cackling laugh.
"Why would I need to care about such things? It's enough to regain the Ghost Legion later."
In other words, the remnants of Seigal were attempting a suicide attack.
It was unclear whether they sincerely believed that the remaining blood relatives and servants in the fortress were worthless, or if they were just boasting that they themselves were invulnerable.
However, it was clear that they were determined to seal the entire fortress.
The swelling bodies of the blood-stained remnants seemed about to burst at any moment.
"Think about who really made the wrong choice in hell!"
Kahahaah, ah, uh, ugh...!
Laks' long laughter suddenly died down.
Red seals were drawn all around, and the bodies of the Seigal remnants twisted and broke, being sucked into them.
The same seal that trapped Smarion was trying to trap the party. Like the clutches of a giant, the red energies were closing in.
Lata and the chiefs reflexively swung their swords at the seal.
Their blades touched, but like water, the cut places quickly returned to their original state.
"My lord! The chiefs and I will try to make a way. Please escape, at least you."
Though it had been only a few days since they became sworn allies, Lata spoke without a moment's hesitation.
"Before the seal recovers, if we keep cutting, there might be a chance for you to escape."
While Lata spoke, Jin was checking the characteristics of the seal. When cut with Aura, it immediately returned as it had with Lata's group, but when using Thunder, the recovery was slower.
With just Thunder, it seemed that they could all escape if they used consecutive secret techniques, but there was no need for that.
'As I felt when Myu-ron Zipfel opened the gates of hell, this kind of thing is best suited for Spirit Energy.'
When he swung Bradamante wrapped in Spirit Energy, the seal was cut like a piece of cloth.
Moreover, unlike the previous ones, even the recovery was extremely slow.
"Lord Lata. There's no need for us to risk our lives together. I'll open the way, let's go."
At those words, Lata and the chiefs realized once again.
In the new era that would open, they were the ones who had undoubtedly grasped the best opportunity first.
